name: Shiraz Shahid Dastghaib International Airport
before:
The main international airport for Fars province and the largest in the south of Iran, at Shiraz. After renovation in 2005 it was rated the second most reliable and modern airport in the country after Tehran Imam Khomeini, on flight safety and navigation systems.

There are two connected passenger terminals. Terminal 1 is the older and larger and handles domestic flights only. Terminal 2 takes all scheduled and charter international services.

That will change. A new international terminal is under construction and was due to be completed by 2024. Once it opens, the current international terminal is to be given over to Hajj flights. Confirm which building applies rather than assuming, because this is still in transition.
after:
The largest airport in the south of Iran, serving Shiraz.

Iran closed its airspace after the United States and Israel struck the country on 28 February 2026. Shiraz was operating again by the end of April, but Iranian airspace can still close at short notice. European regulators tell their airlines not to fly in it at any altitude.

The FCDO advises against all travel to Iran, and the US government tells its citizens not to travel there for any reason.

claims.claim: main international airport for Fars province
claims.wasBefore: The main international airport for Fars province
claims.why: No second source could be reached. Iranian official and news sites time out from here and SKYbrary returns a blank page. The largest-in-the-south claim is kept instead.

claims.claim: rated second most reliable and modern after Tehran Imam Khomeini in 2005
claims.wasBefore: After renovation in 2005 it was rated the second most reliable and modern airport in the country after Tehran Imam Khomeini, on flight safety and navigation systems.
claims.why: Nobody names who made the rating and it dates from 2005. A travel guide gives only a looser version ('the second most advanced one, after IKA'). Of no use to an agent now.

claims.wasBefore: There are two connected passenger terminals.
claims.why: Sources disagree and none is dated: Wikipedia has Terminal 1 for domestic and Terminal 2 for international flights, while the Iran Travel Guide Center says Terminal 1 is for departures and Terminal 2 for arrivals. The airport's own site cannot be reached.

claims.wasBefore: Terminal 1 is the older and larger and handles domestic flights only.
claims.why: As above: disputed, undated, and terminal use during the 2026 disruption is unknown.

claims.wasBefore: Terminal 2 takes all scheduled and charter international services.
claims.why: As above: disputed, undated, and terminal use during the 2026 disruption is unknown.
Introduced the terminal transition, which is cut.

claims.wasBefore: A new international terminal is under construction and was due to be completed by 2024.
claims.why: It did not open by 2024. Search results point to Iranian reports (Mehr News, YJC) that work stalled at about 55 per cent when the contractor stopped and that a new 30-month phase was approved, but those sites time out from here and the Internet Archive is blocked, so nothing could be saved. Cut rather than guessed.

claims.claim: current international terminal to go to Hajj flights
claims.wasBefore: Once it opens, the current international terminal is to be given over to Hajj flights.
claims.why: Depends on the unfinished terminal, and only Wikipedia says so.
